description: Operators that ARE in the esm-spec §4.2 evaluable-core set but that no binding's scalar evaluator has a rule for: a document carrying one must have had it eliminated by an earlier stage (value invention). Each case places the op in the UNTAKEN branch of an `ifelse`, so an evaluator that only raises when evaluation happens to reach the node answers 1.0 instead of refusing. §9.6.6 requires the check to precede evaluation: every binding must refuse each expression with `unevaluable_operator` and name the op. `control` is the counterweight: the same shape with an ordinary operand must still evaluate. A binding with a public scalar expression evaluator (`evaluate`) feeds it `expression` with `bindings`; a binding whose evaluator is built from a model builds `D(u) = expression` with `u` a state and `p` a parameter, and expects the build to refuse.
